name: Satyr Horns
summary: In Ashenvale, Satyr Horns draw dryads seeking vengeance and traders bound for Ratchet. The horns come from satyrs whose corruption has taken root in the ancient forest.

sections.title: Trophies of Vengeance and Commerce
sections.body: Ashenvale’s satyrs bear horns that mark their demonic corruption. At the Shrine of Aessina, the dryad Illiyana gathers them in grief and vengeance for her lost sister Anilia. Pixel, a traveling goblin resting at Splintertree Post, seeks them for trade. Demand for satyr horns has risen in Ratchet, where hunters can sell these remnants of slain demons.

sections.title: Culling the Corrupted Enclaves
sections.body: Satyr Horns must be cut from the beasts themselves; ordinary suppliers do not sell them. Satyrs hold strongholds across Ashenvale, including the corrupted groves of Xavian, the hollows of Satyrnaar, and the ruins of Night Run. Clearing these enclaves drives back the lingering demonic taint and supplies grieving guardians and eager merchants with proof of the cull.

faq.q: Why does Illiyana want Satyr Horns?
faq.answer: Illiyana seeks Satyr Horns to avenge her sister Anilia, whom the satyrs of Ashenvale murdered. The horns show that the satyrs’ numbers are falling and bring peace to Anilia’s spirit.

faq.q: Why is Pixel collecting Satyr Horns?
faq.answer: Pixel, an enterprising traveler staying at Splintertree Post, collects Satyr Horns for the journey to Ratchet. She has learned that they fetch a high price in the goblin port and hires hunters to face the danger before she departs.

faq.q: Where are the best places to find satyrs with these horns?
faq.answer: Satyrs dwell in several corrupted areas of Ashenvale. Many are found in Xavian and Satyrnaar in the northeast, and in Night Run in the east-central forest.

faq.q: What are satyrs, and why do they have horns?
faq.answer: Satyrs are ancient night elves transformed into demonic, beastly beings through pacts made during the War of the Ancients. Their hooves, tails, and horns mark the demonic corruption granted by the Burning Legion.

angles.text: For the kaldorei, taking satyr horns is a bitter duty. It cleanses their ancestral forest of cousins who traded their heritage for demonic service.
From Splintertree Post, Horde warriors clear satyrs threatening their timber operations and sell the horns to goblin buyers bound for Ratchet.
